This week has been full of rumors about Apple's upcoming AirPods with cameras. Here's a summary of all the new information this week about the camera-equipped AirPods Pro.

Latest news on camera-equipped AirPods Pro

It all started on Monday, when someone discovered a video in the macOS 26.7 beta showing AirPods with cameras. In the video, a person wearing AirPods Pro holds up a book and asks Siri to remember the book.

In the video, the camera-equipped AirPods Pro looks almost identical to the existing AirPods Pro 3.

In addition to the video, macOS 26.7 also contains a large amount of code mentioning camera-equipped AirPods, providing more details about how it works.

According to code seen by 9to5Mac, Apple will use a new AccessorySensorMgrd framework to control image capture and other features for the camera-equipped AirPods. In the code, Apple refers to this camera sensor as the "Kino Sensor."

  • Each AirPods Pro has its own camera, designed to capture images simultaneously as a pair. AccessorySensorMgrd will pair the two images together. However, if only one camera captures an image, the framework will produce a blank corresponding image.
  • macOS 26.7 mentions two "capture modes": active and passive. Active mode appears to capture one image from each AirPod, or provide a "capture rate" to continuously transmit images at a specified rate.
  • The framework monitors several factors, including image width and height, pixel binning, left/right X/Y offset, and more.
  • The framework mentions that AirPods Pro will have a privacy indicator light that turns on when the camera is capturing images.

At the same time, a MacRumors forum user also found some details about the AirPods Pro camera resolution:

Active capture mode starts capturing at 640×640 and returns a processed 1024×1024 image. The sampled image data is approximately 0.4 megapixels, while the output image is slightly over 1 megapixel. There is also a lower-resolution passive capture mode that captures at 320×320, which can return 320×320 or 512×512 output depending on the capture mode. The above is the resolution for capture modes; the actual native resolution of the sensor may be larger.

The forum member also had more details about "passive mode," described as "lower resolution and supports environmental awareness." macOS 26 lists five situations that might trigger passive capture:

  • Ambient sound
  • Audio scene changes
  • Posture changes
  • Head movement
  • "Circular area, the user has moved beyond the preset spatial radius."

Release date for camera-equipped AirPods

The appearance of this video and related code in macOS 26.7 beta naturally leads to speculation that this product is about to launch, possibly as early as next month's Apple event alongside the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone Ultra.

However, Bloomberg indicates that this is not the case. In a Wednesday report, Mark Gurman said that the camera-equipped AirPods will still launch in 2027 as planned.

Gurman explained that Apple is developing two versions of this product internally:

  • B790: The version seen in the video. Essentially a modified version of the AirPods Pro 3 with a camera added.
  • B798: The next generation of AirPods (such as AirPods Pro 4), also with a camera added.

Which version Apple will ultimately release remains unclear, but regardless of which one, it won't arrive until at least next year.

Bloomberg's report also reiterated that the AirPods Pro camera will not be able to take photos or videos. Instead, they are designed to "scan the surrounding environment and provide contextual information for the Siri digital assistant and other AI tools."

Summary

Overall, this week has indeed released a lot of new information about camera-equipped AirPods, including their features and operational details.

What do you think about Apple adding cameras to AirPods Pro? Do you think it's a good idea? Feel free to share your thoughts in the comments section.
